predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: the southern part of the Byzantine province of Sardinia, governed from Cagliari by a magistrate after the conquest of 534; infobox Preceded by: Byzantine Empire

successors.name: Republic of Pisa
successors.text: Pisa kept control of Castel di Castro; the Della Gherardesca third is listed here because the infobox names the Republic of Pisa as a successor (the page names the family, not the state)

successors.name: Judicate of Arborea
successors.text: one of the three parts into which the territory was divided, assigned to Arborea

successors.name: Judicate of Gallura
successors.text: one of the three parts, assigned to Gallura

ledger.x: 866: the Judicate of Cagliari appears in Cliopatria's first shape, under a giudice at Santa Igia; the page dates no founding.
1015: Mujahid of Denia lands in Sardinia with 120 ships and occupies the southern coastal plain.
1016: Mujahid flees Sardinia and Pisan and Genoese fleets capture what is left of his ships.
1188: Pisa installs the House of Massa at Cagliari; William I rules 1188-1214.
1206: William I of Cagliari invades Gallura.
1207: Lamberto Visconti marries Elena of Gallura and repulses the Cagliari invasion.
1258: Pisa and the other judicates besiege Santa Igia.
1258: the last battle is lost and the contest ends with the judicate's fall.
1258: Santa Igia falls and the Judicate of Cagliari is divided.

wars.name: Dénia invasion of Sardinia
wars.outcome: Mujahid occupied the southern coastal plain in 1015, beat the judge of Cagliari's army in 1016 and fled in May 1016 when his men mutinied; a storm and the Pisan and Genoese fleets destroyed his ships.

wars.name: Cagliari's invasion of Gallura
wars.outcome: William I of Cagliari invaded Gallura in 1206 and failed; Lamberto Visconti, married to Elena in 1207, repulsed him.

wars.name: William I of Cagliari's wars
wars.outcome: William 'spent his reign (1188-1214) in constant wars with Arborea, Gallura, and Logudoro'; he imprisoned Peter I of Arborea and ruled Arborea in his name, but failed to conquer Gallura.

wars.name: Fall of the Judicate of Cagliari
wars.outcome: In 1256 John allied with Genoa against Pisa and was assassinated; William III succeeded; Pisa and the other judicates besieged Santa Igia in 1258 and the judicate was divided into three parts, Pisa keeping Castel di Castro.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any page opened; the pages give curatoriae and cities only, and Cliopatria's outline follows modern provinces.
